entries.question: What is the current stable release line of Prisma ORM, and is Prisma 8 safe to use in production yet?
entries.answer: Prisma ORM 7 (currently 7.9.1) is the recommended, production-ready release. Prisma 8 is only available as a Release Candidate / Early Access preview, and Prisma explicitly states v7 remains the right choice for production apps.

entries.question: Why is my Prisma Client code no longer appearing in node_modules/@prisma/client after upgrading to Prisma ORM 7?
entries.answer: The new prisma-client generator (the v7 default) requires an explicit output path in the generator block and writes plain TypeScript into your own codebase instead of node_modules - there is no more default/'magic' generation location.

entries.question: Is generator client { provider = "prisma-client-js" } still the right generator to use?
entries.answer: No. prisma-client-js is deprecated and will be removed in a future release; Prisma ORM 7 projects should use provider = "prisma-client", the new Rust-free generator, together with a required output path.

entries.question: Why did my app's bundle size and cold-start time drop so much after upgrading to Prisma 7?
entries.answer: Prisma ORM 7.0.0 (released Nov 19, 2025) removed the Rust query-engine binary and rewrote Prisma Client entirely in TypeScript, cutting client bundle size by about 90% and making queries roughly 3x faster, with better compatibility with edge runtimes like Vercel Edge and Cloudflare Workers.

entries.question: Why does new PrismaClient() now fail without a driver adapter after I upgraded to v7?
entries.answer: Prisma ORM 7 requires a database driver adapter (e.g. @prisma/adapter-pg, @prisma/adapter-better-sqlite3) to construct Prisma Client for every supported database - connecting via just a schema datasource url with no adapter is no longer supported.

entries.question: Where should I configure my DATABASE_URL now that the datasource block's url field is deprecated?
entries.answer: Create a prisma.config.ts file at the project root. Prisma ORM 7 centralizes the database URL, schema path, migrations path, and seed command there, replacing the deprecated url, directUrl, and shadowDatabaseUrl datasource fields.

entries.question: Why isn't my .env file being picked up automatically when I run prisma CLI commands in v7?
entries.answer: Prisma ORM 7 no longer auto-loads environment variables; you must explicitly load them yourself, e.g. import 'dotenv/config' at the top of prisma.config.ts, except on Bun where it isn't necessary.

entries.question: Why do prisma migrate dev --skip-generate and prisma migrate dev --skip-seed fail after upgrading to v7?
entries.answer: Both flags were removed in Prisma ORM 7: --skip-generate was removed from prisma migrate dev and prisma db push, and --skip-seed was removed from prisma migrate dev, with no direct flag replacement.

entries.question: My build fails with module/ESM-related errors after upgrading to Prisma ORM 7 - why?
entries.answer: Prisma ORM 7 ships exclusively as an ES module, so the project needs "type": "module" in package.json plus an ESM-compatible tsconfig (e.g. "module": "ESNext", "moduleResolution": "bundler"), and requires Node.js 20.19.0+ and TypeScript 5.4.0+ as hard minimums.

entries.question: prisma.$use() used to work for my logging/soft-delete middleware - why does it error now?
entries.answer: The Client middleware API ($use) has been removed in Prisma ORM 7; that logic must be migrated to Client Extensions via $extends() with a query component instead.

entries.question: Is the Prisma Metrics preview feature still usable in v7?
entries.answer: No. Metrics was deprecated in Prisma ORM 6.14.0 and has been fully removed in Prisma ORM 7.0.0.

entries.question: Can I run Prisma ORM 7 against a MongoDB database?
entries.answer: Not yet. As of 7.9.1, Prisma ORM v7 does not support MongoDB; projects using MongoDB should stay on Prisma ORM 6 until MongoDB support is added.

entries.question: I have @map on my enum values - does the generated TypeScript enum use the schema name or the mapped DB value in the current Prisma 7?
entries.answer: It uses the schema name, matching v6 behavior. The initial v7.0.0 release briefly switched generated enum values to use the @map value instead, but Prisma reverted that breaking change in v7.3.0 (Jan 21, 2026) after it caused widespread issues for users.

entries.question: What happened to the engineType = "binary" generator option in Prisma 7?
entries.answer: It's gone. The v7 recommended prisma-client generator configuration has no engineType/binary Rust-engine option, since the Rust query-engine binary was removed as part of the v7 rewrite.

entries.question: What does the new compilerBuild generator option do in recent Prisma 7 releases?
entries.answer: Introduced in Prisma ORM v7.3.0, compilerBuild lets you choose between a "fast" Query Compiler build (default, optimized for speed) and a "small" build (optimized for bundle size).

entries.question: Why did prisma db push --accept-data-loss start asking for extra confirmation in mid-2026?
entries.answer: Prisma extended its AI-agent safety checkpoint to cover prisma db push --accept-data-loss (announced July 17, 2026), specifically to prevent AI coding agents from silently applying destructive schema changes.

entries.question: I'm seeing a raw, unhandled driver exception instead of a normal Prisma error for certain queries - is this expected?
entries.answer: It shouldn't be anymore. Since the April 27, 2026 release, previously-unmapped database driver errors surface as a catchable P2039 PrismaClientKnownRequestError instead of crashing the client.

entries.question: Does running prisma migrate dev still automatically execute my seed script in v7 the way it did in v6?
entries.answer: No. Automatic seeding after migrations was removed in Prisma ORM v7; you must explicitly run prisma db seed, with the seed command configured via prisma.config.ts.

entries.question: I saw "native PostgreSQL enum lifecycle management" mentioned for Prisma - is that in the current stable v7 I'm using?
entries.answer: No. That feature, along with stock-Supabase-project compatibility and Row-Level Security policy authoring, is a Prisma 8 Early Access feature announced July 17, 2026; it is not part of the current stable Prisma ORM 7 line.

entries.question: Should I switch my production app to Prisma 8 now for its new TypeScript-schema and SQL query builder features?
entries.answer: Not yet. Prisma 8 is still an Early Access / Release Candidate (e.g. 8.0.0-rc.7) with its own new architecture; Prisma's official guidance is that v7 remains the right, supported choice for production and will keep receiving updates for about 12 months.
